findings.failure_path: Evidence gap: the stat lists changes to guard-merge-authorization.sh, merge-authorization-prompt.sh, guard-edit-isolation.sh, guard-delegation-owner.sh and their tests, but the frozen packet has none of them. The new target-goal grant (repository, numeric target, expiry, single use, no revive after revocation) and Codex patch-path isolation are this release's permission boundary. Neither can be checked, so a scope or replay bypass could ship unreviewed.
findings.smallest_fix: Re-freeze the review packet with the full diffs of these hook scripts and their tests, then re-run the review on the authorization and isolation partition.

findings.failure_path: The 9600-byte budget only replaces the recovery context. If the rendered policy text is over budget by itself (the policy path is interpolated and can be long), the output still exceeds the host's direct-context budget, and the essential rules can be cut off. That contradicts the 'essential rules directly visible' acceptance.
findings.smallest_fix: Also check the byte size of the rendered policy text on its own. If it is over budget, emit a stderr diagnostic, and add a test with a long plugin root path.

concern_results.conclusion: The parts in the packet match their stated acceptance: host-input.py reads patch add, update, delete and move targets and rejects malformed patches, and the doctor inventory requires the complete package-owned hook set. Grant binding and patch path enforcement can't be checked because guard-merge-authorization.sh and guard-edit-isolation.sh aren't in the packet.

Parsing never runs patch or command text, and the inventory never changes trust. Whether edits to the protected checkout are still denied and whether grants are properly scoped depends on hook scripts that are missing from the packet.

The Stop helper stays quiet or sends a static system message when input is bad. The inventory worker has a time limit, an output limit and process-group cleanup. The startup budget only replaces the recovery context; if the policy text alone is over budget, nothing handles it.

The inventory tests and OpenCode install tests are specific and would fail on the risky behavior. The Python tests (test_host_input.py, test_proposed_next.py) and the authorization tests are missing from the packet, so the claimed pass counts can't be checked.

Stop uses the shared decision/reason output. The OpenCode adapter passes a null final message, which leaves the formatter unverified and quiet. The SessionStart matcher adds resume and fork. No compatibility regression is visible.
The version bump to 0.18.2 is consistent across package files. Install never approves trust. Publication is gated in the plan. No irreversible step is in the diff.
Doctor reports distinct hook states with reason codes and runtime=unverified. When the startup budget is exceeded, a warning is written to stderr.

The README and doctor message correctly say that runtime execution is not verified. The plan's statement that grants bind repository, target, expiry and a single use has no supporting code in the packet.
The permission-access boundary is the target-goal merge grant, and its implementation and tests are missing from the packet, so containment can't be checked. Reported as a finding.

No violations visible. The installed name bootstrap.md is kept, and the new session-policy.md is added alongside it. The root AGENTS.md says session-start.md holds the hard rules, but most of them now live in session-policy.md; this is a wording drift, not a defect.
